                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">There are specific provisions e.g. in the general policies, rules and regulations of the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>In signing the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education, the institution agrees to respect <strong>in full</strong> the principles of non-discrimination as set out in the Programme. The institution must clearly demonstrate through its policies, rules and regulations that equal access and opportunities to mobile participants from all backgrounds. Which means that all individuals or groups will be treated equally, irrespective of their characteristics. In accordance with Article 21 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, there should be no discrimination "based on sex, race, colour, ethnic or social origin, genetic features, language, religion or belief, political or any other opinion, membership of a national minority, property, birth, disability, age or sexual orientation". For more information, see: <a href="http://www.europarl.europa.eu/charter/pdf/text_en.pdf">http://www.europarl.europa.eu/charter/pdf/text_en.pdf</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The principle - that extra fees are not being charged to incoming mobile students - is implemented</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The receiving institution must <strong>not </strong>charge any type of fees to incoming mobility students for the tuition, registration or examination of these students or for their access to laboratory, library and other facilities offered to local students.<br>In certain cases, however, mobile students may be required to pay small fees for insurance, student unions, use of miscellaneous materials (e.g. photocopies, laboratory products) on the same basis as these are charged to local students. Students should be made aware of these extra costs before the start of mobility. Fees may only be charged in the case of full degree mobility or for students registered in joint degree programmes.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All students and staff (incoming and outgoing) are treated equally in all academic and service matters</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>In accordance with equal access and opportunities, all students and staff should be treated equally in all academic and service matters. Clear appeal procedures should be in place to ensure equal treatment. There should be individuals - such as mentors and counsellors - available to offer support.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It provides incoming mobile participants with access to the same services and facilities available to local students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is vital to ensure that incoming mobility participants have full access to the same services and facilities as local students and staff. For example, mobility participants with special needs can benefit from the support services that the receiving institution offers to its local students and staff.</p>                      </div>

                        <div class="eche-officer-question">Before the mobility, your institution has established formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to e.g. the use of Learning Agreements)</div>

                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Ensuring that the mobile participant, sending and receiving HEI/organisation/enterprise (i.e. all three parties) sign the Learning Agreement before the start of the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The purpose of the Learning Agreement is to provide a transparent and efficient preparation of the study period abroad and to ensure that the student will receive recognition in his/her degree for the educational components or traineeship successfully completed abroad. The Learning Agreement:</p><ul><li>Sets out the learning outcomes for the mobility, including both the educational components or traineeship activities to be carried out by the student at the receiving institution/organisation/enterprise, which will be recognised by the sending institution upon successful completion of the study programme abroad and counted towards his/her degree.</li><li>Ensures full recognition for satisfactorily completed activities of study mobility and traineeships in terms of credits awarded, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams, and documents these credits in the student records, so that they can be identified in a transparent way.</li></ul><p>The Learning Agreement is binding for all parties and constitutes the cornerstone of successful student mobility (for studies, traineeships, and combinations thereof), including quality assurances and the process for transparent transfer of credits. Therefore, it is essential to conduct mobility based on an agreed and signed Learning Agreement. The Learning Agreement should be agreed and signed by all parties (the student, the sending institution and the receiving institution/organisation/enterprise) before the start of the mobility. It is not compulsory to circulate papers with original signatures; scanned copies of signatures or digital signatures may be accepted, depending on the national legislation.</p><p>The EU official templates for Learning Agreements for studies and traineeships are available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm&nbsp;&nbsp;</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Including allocation of responsibility to an academic who has the authority to approve, amend and recognise the Learning Agreements on behalf of the responsible academic body</span>

                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Incoming mobile students also bring new perspectives to the institution, the local students and the culture which is part of the internationalisation of the receiving institution. This is a significant opportunity to benefit from the experiences that international students bring. To capitalise on these experiences, the institution and its student organisations should put in place opportunities for incoming students to showcase their talent and perspectives through access to existing local initiatives (e.g. school teaching programmes, community projects) and setting up new initiatives to celebrate the different cultures (e.g. theatre performances, food and cultural weeks etc.). Local associations can support the integration of incoming students with the local community, through existing initiatives such as the Social Erasmus and Erasmus in School projects (<a href="http://socialerasmus.esn.org">http://socialerasmus.esn.org</a>).&nbsp;</p><p>Some incoming students may even have been involved in the management or governance of their sending institutions and recognising this opportunity and involving incoming students in similar functions in the receiving institution such as in the student union (elected representative) or working groups dedicated to the voice of the international student.&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>                      </div>

                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include, where applicable, a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Where applicable, the Sending Institution should translate the grades received by the student abroad. To enable the Sending Institution to do so, it is highly important for the receiving institution to provide a clear explanation of the institutional grading system and grade distribution in the department or study programme together with the Transcript of Records. Such information can be provided either through a web link or as an annex to the Transcripts of Records. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>

                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>During a period of mobility, students often take advantage of other opportunities outside of their required courses. These may include specific activities which can be considered non-formal or informal learning where they have acquired new skills. This could include additional language and cultural courses, extra-curricular activities, setting up a business and volunteer work undertaken by the student in that period or upon return at the receiving institution.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/standing-out-from-the-crowd-supporting-students-through-full-recognition-and-documenting-of-mobility-outcomes" target="_blank">"Standing out from the crowd" - supporting students through full recognition and documenting of mobility outcomes</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/a-common-approach-to-ects-grade-conversion-ensuring-a-fair-assessment-of-student-performance-after-study-abroad" target="_blank">A common approach to ECTS grade conversion, ensuring a fair assessment of student performance after study abroad</a></div>

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-diploma-supplement-a-tool-to-promote-international-recognition-and-transparency-of-academic-achievement" target="_blank">The Diploma Supplement – a tool to promote international recognition and transparency of academic achievement</a></div>
                                             </div>

                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">13</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>
                                             </div>

            </div>

                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">

                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Results of cooperation projects are made sustainable and often lead to future stronger international cooperation of the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in European and international cooperation projects should be undertaken in a pro-active way and fully integrated in the HEI's modernisation and internationalisation strategy. Capturing the outcomes and experiences of international cooperation, and disseminating the results provides information which can be fed back into the overall decision making processes of the HEI. These experiences can also be compared to the expected achievements set out in the original strategy documents and can be very important informers of future strategy and sustainability. The strength of the information collected lies in the institution’s approach to reflecting on the outcomes and using the information to further improve and strengthen international cooperation. Therefore the HEI needs to have mechanisms in place which provide a forum to fully reflect on the outcomes and ask questions which will improve the sustainability of international cooperation activities for the benefit of the institution. This implies strategic working groups set at a high level within the institution, whose role is to monitor and implement internationalisation based on evidence in practice</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-erasmus-impact-study-effects-of-mobility-on-the-skills-and-employability-of-students-and-the-internationalisation-of-higher-education-institutions" target="_blank">The Erasmus Impact Study: Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions</a></div>

Job Title: Patient Care Advocate 

Job Location: Remote


About Us: 

We are a dedicated team focused on improving access to affordable prescription medications for patients. By partnering with insurance companies, healthcare providers, and pharmacies, we work to reduce the financial burden of medications, ensuring that patients can access the treatments they need without excessive costs. 


Role Overview: 

As a key member of our team, you will help patients navigate our Prescription Payment Plan. This involves working closely with patients, insurance providers, healthcare professionals, and pharmacies to ensure seamless enrollment, eligibility verification, cost-sharing, and prescription fulfillment. 


What You’ll Do: 

  • Patient Enrollment & Eligibility: Assist patients with enrolling in the program, ensuring all necessary personal and insurance information is provided and verifying eligibility. 
  • Prescription Coverage: Help patients confirm that their prescribed medications are covered under the program, and manage the approval process for eligible medications. 
  • Cost-Sharing & Payment: Reduce patients' out-of-pocket costs by applying the program benefits. Manage copayments, coinsurance, and assist with additional copay assistance when applicable. 
  • Prescription Fulfillment: Coordinate with participating pharmacies to ensure the correct application of benefits during prescription filling, ensuring patients pay the reduced amount. 
  • Refills & Continued Use: Support patients by ensuring they continue receiving medications at reduced costs, monitoring adherence to medication regimens, and ensuring continued eligibility. 
  • Program Renewal & Updates: Guide patients through annual renewals and inform them about any updates to the program or medication formulary. 


What We’re Looking For: 

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Experience in healthcare, insurance or customer service required (experience with prescription assistance programs is a plus)
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to navigate complex processes
  • Excellent communication skills for working with patients, healthcare providers, and pharmacies
  • A genuine passion for helping others and making a positive impact on their healthcare access
  • The ability to work efficiently and collaboratively within a team environment

Success Factors for Working from Home 

  • Private Workspace: A dedicated, quiet workspace with a door that closes, free from ambient noise. 
  • Ergonomics: A comfortable desk and chair setup that allows for the proper installation of necessary equipment. 
  • Reliable Internet Connection: Stable, high-speed internet with a minimum bandwidth of 10 Mbps downstream and 5 Mbps upstream. 
  • Quiet, Distraction-Free Workspace: A dedicated, quiet area where you can focus on delivering excellent customer service without interruptions. 
  • Tech-Savvy: Comfort with technology and ability to learn new systems quickly. 
  • Self-motivation & Independence: Ability to stay productive and manage your time effectively in a remote environment. 
  • Communication Skills: Strong verbal and written communication skills, especially in a virtual setting. 
  • Adaptability: Ability to adapt to changing technologies and procedures while working remotely. 


Compensation & Perks 

  • Hourly Pay: $16.50 per hour 
  • Company-Provided Equipment: All necessary equipment will be provided. 
  • Comprehensive Benefits: Full health insurance package including medical, dental, and vision coverage. 
  • Cell Phone Benefits: $25/month per line for unlimited phone, text, and data (restrictions may apply). 
  • Generous Referral Program: Earn $50 per paycheck for every person you refer—and your referral earns it too! No limits on payouts. 
  • Comprehensive Training: Paid training to ensure you are fully prepared for success. 
  • Career Growth: Opportunities for career advancement and professional development within a leading healthcare provider. 
  • Work-from-Home Convenience: Save time, and money, and reduce your environmental footprint. 
  • Inclusive Culture: We are an Equal Opportunity Employer, including individuals with disabilities and veterans. 

What Success Looks Like: 

  • Reduced out-of-pocket costs for patients through effective cost-sharing and copay assistance 
  • Timely and accurate processing of prescription claims and approvals 
  • High patient satisfaction with the program’s support and streamlined experience 
  • Compliance with program requirements and monitoring of patient eligibility for ongoing assistance 

Why Join Us? 

  • Be part of a team that makes a real difference in patients' lives by reducing the cost of necessary medications 
  • Opportunity for professional growth in the healthcare and insurance sectors 
  • Competitive compensation and benefits package 
  • A collaborative, supportive, and innovative work culture 

Ready to Make an Impact? 

Join us in making prescription medications more affordable and accessible for those who need them most. If you're ready to help make a difference, we'd love to hear from you! 

If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us!

  • Next.js (App Router)

  • Clerk for authentication

Roles & rules

  • user:

    • Can create, edit, and delete only their own listings, and act only on requests involving their own tools or their own borrowing.

  • Implement the above role-based access control with best practices, enforced in Convex functions, not only in the UI.

Automation with n8n

  • Build at least two n8n workflows:

  • Request notification: when a borrow request is created or changes status, Convex calls an n8n Webhook. The workflow notifies the relevant user (email, Slack, Discord, or a logged mock notification is fine) using only the fields it needs.

CAbout the Company

Global University Systems (GUS) is one of the world’s most dynamic, inclusive, and diverse education organisations. GUS is an international network of higher education institutions, brought together by a shared passion for accessible and industry-relevant qualifications. We deliver a wide variety of programmes, including bachelor’s degree programmes, master’s degree programmes, professional training, English Language training, and corporate & executive education. When someone chooses to study at one of our institutions, whether on campus in Europe, North America, Asia or even in their own home, they are joining a network of over 100,000 students worldwide. When you decide to work with GUS, you will be joining an industry leading, global organisation that has a reach in over 150 different countries.

Role Summary

Are you a gifted wordsmith with a knack for transforming ideas into compelling stories that engage audiences and drive action? As a Creative Copywriter at GUS, you will leverage innovative writing techniques and digital tools to captivate our prospective students and meet our organizational goals. We're looking for creative individuals with a passion for excellence and a drive for results.

As a Creative Copywriter, you will contribute to GUS' worldwide content initiatives, harnessing the power of technology and digital platforms to create unique and engaging campaigns that resonate with our brand's ethos. Your work will span across various channels, including organic and paid social media, PPC, SEO and local marketing efforts, harmonizing these elements to build a best-in-class content portfolio.

To excel in this role, you should be an exceptional communicator with a proven ability to conceptualize and implement creative ideas. You should know when to apply technology to accelerate the writing process and when human creativity is essential to the process.

To be an ideal candidate, you will have had extensive experience producing powerful written content for multinational companies. You should be a natural team player who wants to contribute to a creative environment where everyone can produce their best work.

If you're a passionate communicator who is excited by the prospect of shaping the future narratives of our brands and making an impact on a global scale, we invite you to apply for this exhilarating opportunity.

Key Activities and Responsibilities

As a Creative Copywriter at GUS, you will be responsible for:

  • Developing compelling and creative copy for various organic and paid mediums, including social media, PPC, SEO, print and digital campaigns, and email journeys, while ensuring consistency in tone, style, and voice across all platforms and institutions.
  • Utilizing technology and AI tools to enhance the copywriting process, while understanding when a human touch is necessary for the crafting of content.
  • Working in alignment with the overall company's goals and marketing strategies, ensuring that your written content supports these objectives and helps to deliver the desired message to the targeted audience.
  • Staying up to date on the latest trends in content and copywriting, implementing best practices in daily tasks and continuously seeking innovative ways to improve the quality and impact of written content.
  • Working in coordination with the marketing teams to maintain a content calendar that aligns with the company's broader marketing and business goals.
  • Ensuring all content and communication efforts take diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) into consideration.
  • Contributing to content audits on a regular basis to assess the effectiveness of our copywriting efforts, providing useful recommendations for improvements based on key metrics and analysis.
  • Assisting in managing relationships with GUS’ internal brand partners, ensuring clear, persuasive and effective copy is provided for all collaborative efforts.
  • Maintaining a high level of quality control to ensure all produced copy aligns with brand guidelines and is free of errors.

Qualifications and Education

Essential

  • Undergraduate level or equivalent work experience

Desirable

· Digital marketing qualification

· Writing qualification

Experience

  • Significant (5+ years) experience in creative copywriting for multiple channels, including social media, PPC, SEO, content marketing and PR.
  • Demonstrated experience (2+ years) in a team-oriented environment, with the ability to collaborate and contribute to team projects.
  • Strong research and analytical skills, including the ability to understand audience sentiment, analyse content performance and optimize copy based on performance data.
  • An understanding of, and demonstrated interest in, emerging technologies that may impact copywriting including generative AI, automation tools, and data analytics.
  • Strong project management skills, including the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, while ensuring timely execution.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to effectively present ideas to internal stakeholders and collaborate with cross-functional teams.
  • Proven experience working collaboratively with an international team.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to think strategically and creatively to continually improve the company's content and copywriting strategy.
  • Expertise in Microsoft Office, particularly Word and PowerPoint.
  • Fluency in English with excellent writing and editing skills, with a strong grasp of grammar and style.
  • Knowledge of AP Style or other major style guides is a plus.
  • A portfolio of work that demonstrates your writing abilities and creative skills.
  • A demonstrated passion for the educational space
  • Experience with content-related tools and services including SEO tools (such as SEMRush, Ahrefs), social media management tools (such as Buffer, Hootsuite) and content management systems (such as WordPress).
  • Experience in digital marketing including SEO, social media advertising and content marketing.

The post holder may be asked to undertake different or additional duties in line with business requirements at the request of their line manager. There is an expectation that all employees will maintain the values of the Group and will comply with the code of conduct as well as equality and diversity, health and safety and safeguarding policies.

Other information

We acknowledge receipt of your resume for a position at Global University Systems and sincerely appreciate your interest in our company.

Fonemed is redefining how individuals and healthcare organizations connect through secure, cloud-native technology. Our Florizel platform supports a wide range of digital health services and solutions, empowering virtual care delivery across the globe.

We’re seeking a Technical Business Analyst to bridge the gap between clinical and business stakeholders and our software development and quality assurance teams. In this hands-on role, you will translate clinical workflows and business needs into clear, actionable requirements, Jira user stories, acceptance criteria, functional specifications, and test cases that support effective software development and delivery.

Reporting to the Manager of Software Development and Architecture, this role will work closely with development and clinical teams to define, and document foundational requirements of technical solutions often amid quickly evolving or loosely defined criteria.

  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders and external customers to gather, analyze, and clarify business, clinical, and technical requirements, particularly during new client implementations or the development of new capabilities.
  • Develop & document business requirements and clinical workflows and translating them into clear, actionable functional specifications, Jira user stories, and acceptance criteria to guide software development.
  • Create and maintain comprehensive documentation of business processes, system workflows, data flows, integrations, and technical dependencies.
  • Identify and proactively address gaps, ambiguities, risks, dependencies, and scope changes throughout the software development lifecycle.
  • Support QA teams in developing test scenarios, clarifying requirements, investigating defects and validating delivered functionality against acceptance criteria.
  • Participate in Agile development activities, including backlog refinement, sprint planning, sprint reviews, and retrospectives.
  • Collaborate with developers and cloud architects to understand technical constraints involving APIs, system integrations, data, and AWS cloud services.
  • Incorporate applicable healthcare privacy, security, compliance, and patient safety considerations into requirements and technical documentation.
  • Leverage AI tools to improve the efficiency and quality of requirements analysis, documentation, user story development and test case creation while validating outputs and adhering to organizational security and privacy policies.

Qualification & Experience
  • Degree or diploma in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Analysis, Health Informatics, or a related field.
  • 3+ years of experience in business analysis, technical analysis, or a related role within a software development environment.
  • Exceptional written communication and documentation skills, with the ability to translate complex business and technical concepts into clear, actionable specifications.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in requirements gathering, stakeholder engagement, business process analysis, and workflow documentation.
  • Experience writing user stories, acceptance criteria, functional specifications, and supporting test cases.
  • Experience supporting user acceptance testing (UAT), investigating defects, and collaborating with software development and QA teams.
  • Hands-on experience using AI tools to develop and refine requirements, documentation and user stories.
  • Proficiency with Jira and Confluence, or comparable software development management and collaboration platforms.
  • Experience working within Agile/Scrum methodologies and a solid understanding of the software development lifecycle (SDLC).
  • Experience creating process flows and technical diagrams using Lucidchart, Mermaid, or similar platforms.
  • Working knowledge of REST APIs, JSON, and system integrations, with the ability to understand and document technical requirements.

Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience in healthcare, telehealth, or clinical software environments.
  • Experience in a Business Analyst role supporting AI initiatives, including requirements gathering, use case definition, and integration of AI capabilities into business processes and software solutions.
  • Familiarity with healthcare interoperability standards such as HL7/FHIR.
  • Working knowledge of AWS cloud services and cloud-based application architectures.
  • Familiarity with healthcare privacy and regulatory requirements, including HIPAA, PIPEDA, and applicable provincial health information privacy legislation.
  • Familiarity with industry security and compliance frameworks and standards, such as SOC 2, NIST, and ISO/IEC 27001.

Job Description:

Job Duck is seeking a compassionate and detail-oriented Bilingual Intake Specialist to serve as an essential connection between community members and qualified attorneys. In this role, you will conduct high volume phone and web based intake, evaluate legal service needs, coordinate referrals, and guide clients through the consultation process using clear and reassuring language. You will make a meaningful daily impact by helping individuals understand their options while ensuring accurate records, timely follow-up, and a professional client experience. The ideal candidate communicates fluently in English and Spanish, remains composed when assisting people facing stressful situations, and exercises sound judgment without providing legal advice. This opportunity is well suited for someone who values public service, enjoys collaborative work, and is motivated to improve access to justice.


• Compensation Range: $1,142 to $1,220

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Maintain patience and professional boundaries when assisting repeat callers or individuals with complex concerns.
  • Perform additional administrative and office responsibilities as assigned
  • Translate complex legal terminology into plain language that clients can understand.
  • Review call recordings to identify opportunities for improving intake quality and the client experience.
  • Track metrics including call volume, referral rates, declined referrals, reassigned matters, and follow-up completion.
  • Maintain professional communication and records with referral partners and legal service organizations.
  • Review Spanish translations of website content and client materials for clarity and accuracy.
  • Recommend practical improvements to intake, referral, and follow-up procedures.
  • Assist with the preparation of accurate recurring reports.
  • Screen clients for financial eligibility for reduced fee and pro bono legal service programs.
  • Record successful referrals, reassignments, and follow-up activity in the case management system.
  • Send referral confirmations to clients and attorneys and verify receipt when appropriate.
  • Determine whether a matter may be referred to a qualified panel attorney based on established procedures.
  • Conduct complete client intake in English and Spanish, including intake for clients who communicate exclusively in Spanish
  • Schedule paid consultations and process related payments accurately.
  • Ask focused questions to identify the caller’s legal concern, applicable practice area, urgent dates, deadlines, and relevant court information.
  • Direct callers to appropriate government agencies, social service organizations, or legal service providers when an attorney referral is unavailable.
  • Explain the consultation process, applicable fees, referral information, and next steps in clear, accessible language without providing legal advice.
  • Review and respond to online referral requests within established timeframes.
  • Keep clients informed of referral reassignments and follow up until consultations are confirmed.
  • Monitor self-referral bookings and reassign declined referrals to another qualified panel attorney within one business day.
  • Answer calls from the legal referral phone queue promptly and professionally while managing more than 20 calls per day.
  • Contact attorneys’ offices to place eligible cases and communicate relevant facts, dates, and court information
  • Contact applicants to obtain missing information and complete the required screening process.
  • Maintain accurate and detailed records for every intake, referral, reassignment, payment, and follow-up.
  • Support monthly registration activities for legal access clinics.

Requirements:

• Full professional fluency in English and Spanish, including spoken and written communication and the ability to conduct complete client intake in Spanish

• Familiarity with legal terminology in both English and Spanish

• Previous experience in legal intake, client services, call center operations, or a comparable high volume service environment

• Availability to work Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Pacific Time

• Ability to manage more than 20 calls per day while maintaining accuracy, professionalism, and appropriate follow-up

• Experience using or the ability to quickly learn Qase for case management and customer relationship management

• Experience using or the ability to quickly learn GoTo Connect or Microsoft Teams for phone communications

• Proficiency with Microsoft 365, particularly Outlook and Teams, for email, calendaring, and internal communication

• Reliable computer equipment, a stable internet connection, and a professional environment suitable for handling confidential client calls

• Understanding that the position provides referral information and procedural guidance but does not provide legal advice

AllCloud is seeking an Services Account Executive to support the sale of professional services associated with the Salesforce platform. In this role, you will generate new business opportunities through proactive prospecting, and you will partner closely with senior Account Executives to help develop and grow existing client accounts. This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career sales professional to build a foundation in consultative, solution-based selling within a fast-growing cloud services practice, while receiving direct mentorship from experienced enterprise sellers.

Channel, Delivery & Thought Leadership

  • Salesforce Channel Relationships: Build and maintain relationships with Salesforce Account Directors, communicate account updates, and help identify co-sell and whitespace opportunities.

Experience

  • 1-3 years of entry-level professional experience, internships, or a background in basic sales, client support, or lead generation.

  • Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills to pitch services and engage with clients.

TransPerfect is sourcing this role on behalf of our client, a contract research organization (CRO). Candidates will apply through TransPerfect.

Position Overview

  • Type: Full-time, 12-month contract-to-hire

  • Location: US-based and remote. There is no specific home location requirement.

  • Travel: Periodic site visits. Candidates must be able to visit Midwest clinical sites, especially during study startup, so travel flexibility is required.

  • Openings: One Clinical Trial Manager (CTM) for two studies expected to begin in early January.

Key Responsibilities

Study Start-Up and Feasibility

  • Evaluate new studies with the Principal Investigator (PI). Assess protocol feasibility, patient population, staffing, equipment, and space.

  • Complete Sponsor and CRO feasibility questionnaires. Take part in pre-study and site qualification visits.

  • Prepare and submit IRB applications, informed consent forms, amendments, continuing reviews, and safety reports.

  • Coordinate review of Clinical Trial Agreements (CTAs) and Confidentiality Agreements with clinic leadership and legal counsel.

  • Develop and negotiate study budgets with Sponsors. This includes per-patient costs, start-up fees, and pass-through expenses.

  • Lead site initiation visits. Activate the site only after all approvals, training, and supplies are in place.

Study Conduct and Oversight

  • Oversee day-to-day conduct of all active studies. Ensure compliance with the protocol, GCP, FDA regulations, HIPAA, and clinic policies.

  • Oversee participant recruitment, screening, consent, enrollment, scheduling, and retention. Develop recruitment strategies suited to the clinic's patient population.

  • Verify that informed consent is properly obtained and documented before any study procedures.

  • Ensure source documentation and EDC data entry are accurate and timely. Oversee query resolution.

  • Ensure adverse events, serious adverse events, and protocol deviations are documented and reported to the PI, Sponsor, and IRB on time.

  • Oversee investigational product accountability: receipt, storage, dispensing, temperature monitoring, and return or destruction.

  • Oversee specimen collection, processing, storage, and shipment per lab manuals, including staff shipping training.

  • Act as primary contact for Sponsors, CROs, and monitors. Host monitoring visits and resolve findings promptly.

Regulatory and Quality

  • Maintain inspection-ready regulatory binders and electronic files for each study. These include Form FDA 1572s, delegation logs, financial disclosures, CVs, licenses, and training records.

  • Ensure all research staff hold current GCP, human subjects protection, and protocol-specific training. Ensure the PI delegates responsibilities appropriately.

  • Maintain and update clinic research SOPs, templates, and work instructions.

  • Prepare the clinic for Sponsor audits and FDA or other regulatory inspections. Lead development and tracking of corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs).

  • Ensure applicable studies are registered and updated on ClinicalTrials.gov, as directed.

Financial and Administrative Management

  • Track study budgets, invoiceable items, and Sponsor payments. Ensure timely invoicing and reconciliation.

  • Support research billing compliance by separating routine-care charges from research-related charges, in coordination with billing staff.

  • Prepare enrollment, financial, and performance reports for the PI and clinic leadership.

  • Manage study supplies, equipment calibration and maintenance records, and vendor relationships.

Team Leadership

  • Hire, train, schedule, supervise, and evaluate Clinical Research Coordinators and other research staff.

About Us

Live Oak Bank is a digital bank for small business owners across the country. Our goal is to be America’s Small Business Bank, and we’re getting there by pairing exceptional service with smart technology. We support owners at every stage with products:

  • loans to buy, build, and expand
  • checking and merchant services to keep daily operations moving
  • high-yield savings and CDs to grow the money they’ve worked hard to earn

Our people are the heart of Live Oak. We take care of each other here, and that care carries over to how we serve our customers. If you want to help small business owners chase the American dream, we’d love to meet you.


How This Role Impacts Live Oak and its People

The Senior Credit Officer, Commercial (Solar & Renewable Energy) is the embedded credit officer for the Bank’s solar and renewable energy lending team. This role approves solar and renewable energy credit requests within individual loan authority, adhering to Bank policies and Government program guidelines, and serves as the primary credit partner to Energy & Infrastructure bankers and underwriters from early deal structuring through approval, closing, construction, and ongoing portfolio management. They lead the credit review of the Bank’s solar and renewable energy portfolio to help prevent or reduce loan losses. Responsibilities include verifying that documentation aligns with loan approvals and regulatory requirements, identifying early signs of project, sponsor, or counterparty deterioration, and ensuring compliance with policy objectives. As capacity allows, this role also supports loan transactions and portfolio activities across other Commercial Bank lending verticals.


Location Preference: This position is ideally based in Wilmington, NC; however, remote designations may be considered for qualified candidates.

What You’ll Do at Live Oak

  • Serve as the embedded credit officer for the solar and renewable energy lending team, engaging with bankers and underwriters early in the deal process to shape structure, terms, and risk mitigants before transactions reach approval
  • Approve solar and renewable energy credit requests within individual authority, adhering to Bank and regulatory guidelines (FDIC, SBA, and USDA), and present larger or more complex transactions to the Commercial Finance Credit Committee and senior credit leadership
  • Provide subject matter expertise on solar and renewable energy projects and financing structures, including utility-scale, community solar, commercial and industrial (C&I), and battery energy storage (BESS) projects across construction, term, bridge, and tax credit related financings
  • Evaluate project economics and revenue quality, including PPA, offtake, and community solar subscription contracts, merchant and REC exposure, independent engineer reports, energy production estimates (P50/P99), degradation and availability assumptions, and debt sizing and DSCR sculpting
  • Assess sponsor, developer, EPC, and O&M counterparty strength, along with construction completion risk, interconnection and permitting status, equipment supply and warranty coverage, and tax credit (ITC/PTC) eligibility, transferability, and recapture considerations in light of evolving federal tax, tariff, and trade policy
  • Oversee the credit aspects of construction lending and conversion to term, including draw review, milestone and COD tracking, and satisfaction of conversion conditions, in partnership with construction risk and servicing teams
  • Own credit oversight of the solar and renewable energy portfolio, including monitoring project performance against base case, covenant and reserve compliance, annual reviews, and accurate risk ratings
  • Identify early warning signs on solar and renewable energy credits and lead resolution strategy on watch list and troubled loans in partnership with Servicing and Special Assets
  • Approve modifications, waivers, consents, and extensions on existing solar and renewable energy loans within individual authority
  • Contribute to solar and renewable energy credit policy, underwriting standards, and concentration monitoring, and prepare portfolio reporting for senior management, the Board, and regulators
  • Conduct site visits to operating and under-construction projects
  • Support loan production while ensuring compliance with all applicable risk policies, procedures, and mitigants
  • Contribute to the collaborative process that aims to produce sound credit decisions and add appropriately structured loans to support the Bank’s growth and loan generation goals
  • Work cross-functionally with departments involved in loan production to ensure smooth execution
  • Assist with broader Credit Team functions (credit training, board reports, credit policy maintenance, and participation in the Commercial Finance Credit Committee)
  • As capacity allows, support loan transactions and portfolio activities across other Commercial Bank lending verticals, including Seniors Housing, ABL/GovCon, Sponsor Finance, Venture Banking, and broader Energy & Infrastructure
  • Maintain a high standard of regulatory awareness including BSA, AML, CIP, and OFAC

Required Experience

  • 7+ years of solar and renewable energy credit experience, including financial analysis, underwriting, structuring, and credit approval of project-level and portfolio financings
  • Demonstrated experience decisioning or recommending credit approvals on solar and renewable energy transactions, including construction and term financings
  • Working knowledge of solar and renewable energy project documents (PPAs, interconnection agreements, EPC and O&M contracts, independent engineer reports, and tax equity and tax credit transfer structures) and the financial models used to size project debt
  • Experience managing a renewable energy loan portfolio, including risk rating, covenant monitoring, and problem loan resolution
  • Strong understanding of the Bank’s policies, procedures, and criteria
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including presenting credit recommendations to committee
  • Commercial lending and sales experience; exposure to other Commercial Bank verticals (commercial real estate, sponsor finance, venture banking, or ABL) and to USDA or SBA guaranteed lending programs is a plus

 

Our Values

  • Dedication: Possess a deep commitment to Live Oak Bank’s mission and core values, exemplified through a strong work ethic, adaptability and pride in your work.

  • Ownership: Take initiative to deliver positive results by proactively and creatively solving problems, while maintaining a high degree of quality.

  • Respect: Treat everyone with courtesy, politeness, and kindness.

  • Innovation: Embrace fresh ideas and fearlessly contribute new solutions to emerging or existing problems.

  • Teamwork: Foster collaboration, accountability, and trust with others and understand that together, we do more

<p>

</p>

<p>Werde zum Architekten digitaler Finanzwelten – und gestalte mit uns die Zukunft! Zahlen sind Deine Leidenschaft, die Financial Supply Chain und SAP FI/CO Dein Spielfeld? Perfekt! Denn als Consultant wirst Du:</p>
<h2>Aufgaben</h2>
<p>Digitale Finanzwelten erschaffen – Du berätst und implementierst SAP FI/CO-Lösungen, die unsere Kunden begeistern</p>
<ul>
<li>Geschäftsprozesse neu denken – Du analysierst, designst und revolutionierst Finanzprozesse</li>
<li>Wissen teilen und multiplizieren – In Deinen Workshops und Schulungen machst Du aus Anwendern echte Power-User</li>
<li>Konzepte entwickeln, die beeindrucken – Deine Fachkonzepte sind so klar wie durchdacht</li>
<li>Bestehende Lösungen auf das nächste Level heben – Du entwickelst SAP- und BDF-Lösungen kontinuierlich weiter</li>
</ul>
<h2>Qualifikation</h2>
<p>Du bist unser Perfect Match, wenn Du:</p>
<ul>
<li>Einen Abschluss in BWL, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation in der Tasche hast</li>
<li>Mindestens 3 Jahre Erfahrungen als SAP FI/CO-Berater gesammelt hast</li>
<li>Die SAP-Module FI und CO oder FSCM bereits kennst und Dich dort weiter einarbeiten möchtest</li>
<li>Erfahrungen im SAP-Customizing sammeln konntest</li>
<li>Komplexe Zusammenhänge schnell erfasst und in klare Konzepte übersetzt</li>
<li>Nicht nur mit Zahlen, sondern auch mit Menschen hervorragend kommunizieren kannst</li>
<li>Auf Deutsch und Englisch überzeugst – egal ob in Meetings oder Dokumentationen</li>
<li>Den Kunden immer in den Mittelpunkt stellst und flexibel auf Anforderungen reagierst</li>
<li>Bereit bist, gelegentlich zu reisen (keine Sorge, wir schicken Dich nicht auf Weltreise)</li>
<li>Erfahrungen und Interesse an der Erarbeitung von KI Use Cases hast</li>
</ul>
<h2>Benefits</h2>
<p><strong>Bei uns erwartet Dich mehr als nur ein Job:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Abwechslung garantiert!</strong> Kein Tag gleicht dem anderen in unserem dynamischen Team</li>
<li><strong>Work-Life-Balance leben</strong> mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten und Homeoffice-Möglichkeiten</li>
<li><strong>Wachse über Dich hinaus</strong> durch individuelle Weiterbildungen, die zu Dir passen</li>
<li><strong>Ideen statt Hierarchien</strong> – bei uns zählt Dein Input, nicht Dein Titel</li>
<li><strong>Gestalte aktiv mit</strong> und sieh, wie Deine Ideen Wirklichkeit werden</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Heute Consultant, morgen...? Bei uns kannst Du:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Einen langfristigen Karriereweg einschlagen – vielleicht als zukünftiger Projektleiter oder Solution Specialist</li>
<li>Teil eines Unternehmens sein, das in den Bereichen Controlling, Corporate Finance und Treasury Management Maßstäbe setzt</li>
<li>Mit Deinem Know-how direkt zum Unternehmenserfolg beitragen</li>
</ul>
<p>Dann lass uns reden! Erzähle uns in einem kurzen Motivationsschreiben, warum Du perfekt in die BDF-Familie passt, und bewirb Dich noch heute!</p>
<p><strong>Deine Ansprechpartnerin</strong><br>Karin van Soest</p>
<p><strong>P.S.:</strong> Wir freuen uns darauf, Dich kennenzulernen – und gemeinsam die digitale Zukunft zu gestalten!</p>

      <category>Front-End Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Remote (US)
</p>

<h3>&nbsp;</h3>
<h2><strong>About the Role</strong></h2>
<p>As a Freelance Marketo Email Specialist, you'll build, test, and launch email programs in Marketo for a range of client brands. This is a hands-on, execution-only contract role with no leadership or management responsibilities. You'll take approved briefs and turn them into working programs, building responsive templates and modules, setting up smart lists and flows, and making sure every send goes out right the first time. You know Marketo well enough to spot a broken token, a misfired trigger, or a segmentation gap before it reaches a subscriber. You'll take direction from our internal team, get up to speed fast, and deliver accurate builds on schedule with minimal oversight.</p>
<h2><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li>Build and launch email programs in Marketo, including one-off sends, nurture streams, engagement programs, and triggered campaigns.</li>
<li>Develop and maintain responsive email templates and modular components in HTML and CSS, using Marketo's template syntax, variables, and editable sections.</li>
<li>Set up smart lists, smart campaigns, flow steps, and segmentations that match the targeting and logic in the brief.</li>
<li>Use tokens, dynamic content, and snippets to personalize emails and keep programs easy to clone and reuse.</li>
<li>QA every email before launch: rendering across clients and devices (e.g. Litmus or Email on Acid), links, tokens, personalization fallbacks, and list logic.</li>
<li>Manage program structure, naming conventions, and folder organization so client instances stay clean and easy to navigate.</li>
<li>Build to the brief and requirements provided, and flag any gaps or errors in the request before they become problems in the send.</li>
<li>Communicate status, timelines, and blockers clearly with your internal point of contact.</li>
<li>Document builds and processes so other team members can pick up, update, or reuse the work.</li>
<li>Follow established Marketo, deliverability, and accessibility standards on every build.</li>
</ul>
<h2><strong>Qualifications</strong></h2>
<h3><strong>Required</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>At least 3 years of hands-on experience building and deploying email campaigns in Marketo Engage.</li>
<li>Strong working knowledge of Marketo programs, smart lists, smart campaigns, tokens, snippets, and dynamic content.</li>
<li>Proficiency in HTML and CSS for email, including responsive and hybrid coding and Marketo template syntax.</li>
<li>Experience with email rendering and QA tools such as Litmus or Email on Acid.</li>
<li>A detail-oriented QA process that catches errors in logic, links, and personalization before launch.</li>
<li>Experience working across multiple clients or Marketo instances, adapting quickly to different setups and conventions.</li>
<li>Clear, proactive communication, including flagging risks early and giving accurate time estimates.</li>
<li>Ability to work independently, take direction well, and hit deadlines across overlapping requests.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>Preferred</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>Marketo Certified Expert or Marketo Certified Associate.</li>
<li>Familiarity with email deliverability, authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), and list hygiene.</li>
<li>Experience with email accessibility standards (e.g. WCAG).</li>
<li>Experience with lead scoring, lifecycle programs, and Marketo–Salesforce CRM sync.</li>
<li>Experience with other marketing automation platforms (e.g. Salesforce Marketing Cloud, HubSpot, Braze).</li>
<li>Agency or consulting experience.</li>
</ul>
<h2><strong>Why Current</strong></h2>
<p>At Current, we believe the best digital work happens when strategy, design, production, and technology operate as one team. We partner with ambitious brands to create digital experiences that are thoughtful, scalable, and built to drive real impact.</p>
<p>We're a remote-first agency with teams across the US, working collaboratively across websites, platforms, campaigns, CRM ecosystems, and digital product experiences. Our environment is fast-paced, highly collaborative, and built for people who enjoy solving complex technical challenges alongside smart, supportive teammates.</p>
<p>You'll have the opportunity to work across a variety of clients and technologies, and contribute to meaningful digital experiences within a growing agency environment.</p>
<p>This is a freelance, contract engagement. The target hourly rate for this role is $50 - $70 per hour. Actual rate is influenced by a wide array of factors, including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and location.</p>

<p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/current-freelance-marketo-email-engineer">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/current-freelance-marketo-email-engineer</a></p>
</description>
